newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets Deng memorial ceremony for Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: China sets Deng memorial ceremony for Tuesday.

text.p: More than 10,000 people will gather in Beijing's cavernous Great Hall of the People for a memorial ceremony for China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, the Funeral Committee announced on Thursday.

His widow and children sent a letter to his anointed heir, Communist Party chief and state President Jiang Zemin, saying that Deng wanted to donate his corneas to an eye bank, to give his body for medical research and have his ashes scattered at sea.

The memorial on the morning of February 25 in the Great Hall of the People in central Beijing would be attended by 10,000 people but the ceremony would not include a lying in state of Deng's body with mourners filing past, the committee said.
"Comrade Xiaoping always believed in simple and frugal funerals, and it is in keeping with his ideas that no farewell ceremony be held," the letter from his family said.
The family requested that the memorial be held after the cremation, with the casket covered by a flag of the Communist Party of China.
"No ashes should be preserved," the family wrote. "It is the wish of Comrade Xiaoping himself that his ashes be cast into the sea.

The Funeral Committee announced a memorial that would reduce the pomp to a minimum but would not include a ceremony to pay last respects to his remains -- in accordance with Deng's wishes for a simple final goodbye.
Deng always eschewed the cult of personality that surrounded his predecessor Mao Zedong and had said he wanted a simple memorial ceremony.

However, whistles on trains, ships, warships, or in factories would be blown for three minutes in mourning at 10.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) on the morning of the ceremony as the memorial meeting begins, the committee said.
That is the same sign of respect that accompanied the memorial ceremony for Mao when he died in September 1976.

On the day of the ceremony, China's bright red flag emblazoned with five gold stars would be flown at half-mast at all party, government, and military offices, at air and sea ports, at enterprises, institutions, and schools, and at China's embassies around the world, the committee said.
"The memorial meeting for Deng Xiaoping in the capital is an event for the whole Party, the whole military, and the people... to express their grief," it said.
The ceremony would be attended by 10,000 people from party, government and military but no foreign visitors were invited.
"Comrade Xiaoping has devoted his entire life to the motherland and the people without any reservation," his family wrote in the letter signed by his widow, two sons and three daughters.
"We hope that the last thing we do for him will reflect the essence of his mental outlook, and express our grief in an utterly plain and solemn way," it said.
Deng's final journey would differ sharply from that of Mao, whose mummified body lies encased in a glass sarcophagus in a mausoleum in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, open to visitors each morning.
